title: Coefficient compatibility square for the actual projection mate
statement:
In the standing separated finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism and $a:R\to S$ a map of commutative condensed rings such that scalar extension is exact on every scheme. In the ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories put $T_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$, $P_R=Lf_R^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$, and similarly for $S$. Let $c_f:T_XP_R\cong P_ST_Y$ and $\gamma_f:T_YG_R\to G_ST_X$ be the specified comparisons [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso, def-sfb-derived-push-hom]. Let $\mu_Z:T_Z(A\otimes_R^LB)\cong T_ZA\otimes_S^LT_ZB$ be the canonical scalar tensor comparison. For $K\in D(R_X),M\in D(R_Y)$ put $H=K\otimes_R^LP_RM$, and let $\pi^R,\pi^S$ be the projection morphisms [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Then, with rightmost map applied first,
$$\pi^S_{T_XK,T_YM}\circ(\gamma_{f,K}\otimes1)\circ\mu_Y
=G_S((1\otimes c_{f,M})\circ\mu_X)\circ\gamma_{f,H}\circ T_Y(\pi^R_{K,M}).$$
Both sides run from $T_Y(G_RK\otimes_R^LM)$ to $G_S(T_XK\otimes_S^LP_ST_YM)$. No properness, constructibility, or invertibility of a projection or push comparison is assumed.

Identify the conjugate of coefficientScalarPathIso directly with derivedComapLowerStarIso inverse: apply the proved right-derived composition/conjugation theorem to each path, cancel the common composition comparison, and transport the exact left and right functors through their canonical derived-versus-levelwise isomorphisms. The proved source-library theorem rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso_eq_viaRightDerived identifies the two exact-postcomposition comparisons. Unfolding derivedComapLowerStarIso now gives precisely its inverse, without the ringed-square normalization theorem. Injectivity of conjugation gives coefficientScalarPathIso = derivedPullIso inverse. Substitute into the tensor equation and cancel the isomorphism on the tensor input to obtain ComparisonCompatible for the actual tensorators.

proof.text:
The definitions [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso, def-sfb-derived-push-hom, def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso, def-sfb-mate-push-hom] give the following counit equation:
$$\varepsilon^S_{T_XK}P_S(\gamma_K)=T_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\sigma_{G_RK}.\tag{2}$$
Here is the calculation, including the relation between the two different mates. Put $U=D(\mathrm{Res}_{a_X})$, $V=D(\mathrm{Res}_{a_Y})$, and write $\eta^X,v^X,v^Y$ for the scalar unit on $X$ and scalar counits on $X,Y$. The mate definition says $\gamma_K=v^Y_{G_ST_XK}T_Y(e^{-1}_{T_XK})T_YG_R(\eta^X_K)$. Conjugacy for the composite adjunctions, whose counits are those of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], says
$$\varepsilon^S_B P_S(v^Y_{G_SB})P_ST_Y(e^{-1}_B)=v^X_BT_X(\varepsilon^R_{UB})\sigma_{G_RUB}.$$
Substitute $B=T_XK$ and precompose with $P_ST_YG_R(\eta^X_K)$. Naturality of $\sigma$ moves this last map to $T_XP_RG_R(\eta^X_K)$; naturality of $\varepsilon^R$ turns $\varepsilon^R_{UT_XK}P_RG_R(\eta^X_K)$ into $\eta^X_K\varepsilon^R_K$. Finally $v^X_{T_XK}T_X(\eta^X_K)=1$ is the scalar adjunction triangle. This proves (2). The adjunction bijection therefore identifies $\gamma$ with the geometric mate of $\sigma$.

Apply [lem-sp-categorical-projection-mate-square] with $F=P_R$, $G=G_R$, $F'=P_S$, $G'=G_S$, $N_D=T_Y$, $N_C=T_X$, $\alpha=\sigma$, $\varphi=d^R$, $\varphi'=d^S$, and $m_Z=\mu_Z$. Equation (1), precomposed with $\sigma_{A\otimes B}^{-1}$, is exactly its ComparisonCompatible hypothesis; Step 2 identifies its mate $\beta$ with $\gamma$. By [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map] its adjoint-transpose projection maps are the specified $\pi^R,\pi^S$. Its equality, with $\alpha^{-1}=c$ and the two sides exchanged, is the claimed square. No projection or push comparison was cancelled.
